thread:
inc-bot: ALERT: REGION_FAILOVER_DETECTED — multiple region health checks indicate degraded dataplane in us-west-1. severity=P2. paging oncall.

oncall-li: taking the page. seeing spikes in 5xx and request timeouts for edge->backend in us-west-1c. marking incident and joining bridge.

ken-sre: Confirming. Error rate up ~18% for a subset of routes. Some traffic appears to be shifted to us-east-1 but the orchestration shows a partial shift state.

syed-net: Observed abnormal BGP churn from us-west-1c to our transit fabric. A subset of prefixes flapped between POPs causing asymmetric ingress/egress.

oncall-li: Is the failover controller doing a gradual shift or immediate cut? need the controller logs.

alina-platform: Pulling controller logs now — shows failover begun at 3150004200, pause requested, then resumed briefly; drain did not complete before routes flipped back. Looks like a race between health policy and the drain watchdog.

ken-sre: Here's the controller excerpt (sanitized):
```
[3150004200] trigger failover region=us-west-1 status=start 
[3150004222] drain start nodes=12 
[3150004238] healthcheck still failing, resume routing to fallback us-east-1 partial=true 
[3150004245] drain aborted due to route change
```

syed-net: Running quick mtr from POP->backend in us-west-1c shows packet loss after the third hop.
```
mtr -rwc 100 backend-west-1c
Loss%  Last  Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
 40.0  120ms 110ms  12ms  500ms 75ms
```

support-ram: Support is getting multiple tickets from customers in the west region. Two large customers report elevated errors and one has already started failing over on their side. I advised them we're investigating.

pm-olivia: Flagging downstream product teams and account execs. This looks like it could be customer-impacting for west-coast latency-sensitive apps.

oncall-li: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable automatic failover automation for us-west-1 to stop oscillation 2) set routing to sticky for 15m for affected services 3) open ticket with cloud provider for AZ-level network instability 4) prepare capacity uplift in us-east-1 if we need controlled cutover.

alina-platform: Executing step 1:
```bash
redwoodctl orchestration set --region us-west-1 --auto_failover false --note "pause due to bgp flap"
```

oncall-li: Confirmed. auto_failover=false.

syed-net: Cloud NOC ticket CN-49012 opened. They acknowledge aggregation switch in us-west-1c saw interface flaps and are rolling a hardware remediation. ETA unknown. Asking them to place the AZ under maintenance mode.

ken-sre: Step 2: applying sticky routing for services matching `api-*` and `ingest-*`:
```bash
redwoodctl routing update --selector "service in (api-*,ingest-*)" --region us-west-1 --mode sticky --duration 15m
```

alina-platform: Routing update applied. Monitoring for 5xx drop. Also lowering retry aggressiveness to avoid cross-region amplification: `retries.max=1` for affected selectors.

support-ram: Errors down to ~6% now from 18%. Some tail latencies still present for requests that had previous cached routes. Customers updated; safety note on status page.

syed-net: Cloud NOC pushed a fix and reports the flaps have ceased. They recommend we wait ten minutes post-convergence before re-enabling automation.

oncall-li: Agreed. We'll wait 10m and then perform a controlled re-enable. If any signs of re-flapping, we escalate to full cutover plan.

ken-sre: Doing a global route cache clear for affected prefixes to avoid stale route reuse:
```bash
redwoodctl cache flush --scope route --filter "region=us-west-1 and service in (api-*,ingest-*)"
```

alina-platform: Cache flush acknowledged. Also creating a short-lived capacity reservation in us-east-1 in case we need to move load: `capacity.reserve --region us-east-1 --gpu 8 --dur 2h`

pm-olivia: Coordinating communications: support to send another customer update in 20m. Product wants a quick post-incident briefing.

oncall-li: Logging actions and will create the incident ticket for RCA. Oncall handing to ken-sre in 30 minutes for follow-up and postmortem. Thanks team.

support-ram: Customers acknowledged update. One asks for compensation policy; forwarded to account team.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity=P3 — partial recovery, monitoring. Next update scheduled in 10m or on new event."
